matchstick.title: Balance by numeric difference and single‑stick transformation
matchstick.principle: Before moving any stick, compute the numeric values of both sides (including any arithmetic) to determine the numeric imbalance. Then look for a single‑stick transformation that can adjust the imbalance to zero.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever the equation is false and you need to decide which stick to move, start by evaluating both sides and the numeric difference.
matchstick.example: Moving a stick arbitrarily without first checking the numeric difference, leading to a transformation that does not correct the imbalance.

matchstick.title: Convert V to X to add 5
matchstick.principle: If the numeric imbalance is exactly 5 and a V appears on the side that must increase, move one of the V’s sticks to change it into an X, increasing its value by 5.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to increase a side by 5 and a V is present on that side.
matchstick.example: Attempting to move a stick from a V but ending up with an invalid shape that is not an X.

matchstick.title: Transfer I stick between numerals
matchstick.principle: Move a vertical I‑stick from a numeral that contains at least one I to another numeral that can accept an additional I, decreasing the source value by 1 and increasing the target value by 1.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the imbalance is a multiple of 1 and there are I’s available to move without invalidating the source numeral.
matchstick.example: Removing the only I from a solitary I numeral, leaving it empty.

matchstick.title: Swap '-' and '=' by moving a horizontal stick
matchstick.principle: If both a minus sign (single horizontal) and an equals sign (two horizontals) are present, you can move one horizontal stick from the equals sign to the minus sign, turning the minus into an equals and the equals into a minus.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to change a minus into an equals (or vice versa) and both operators are present.
matchstick.example: Moving a horizontal from the equals sign and leaving only one horizontal, making the equality sign invalid.

matchstick.title: Ensure a valid '=' remains when moving a stick from '='
matchstick.principle: When taking a stick away from the equality sign, make sure the remaining sticks still form a valid '=', i.e., keep two horizontal sticks; otherwise the equation loses its equality operator.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Any time you consider moving a stick from the equals sign.
matchstick.example: Taking a horizontal from '=', resulting in a single horizontal line (a minus) instead of a valid equals.

matchstick.title: Convert X to V to subtract 5
matchstick.principle: If the numeric imbalance is exactly 5 and an X appears on the side that must decrease, move one of the X’s diagonal sticks to change it into a V, decreasing its value by 5.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to reduce a side by 5 and an X is present on that side.
matchstick.example: Removing a diagonal from an X and leaving a single diagonal, which is not a valid numeral.

matchstick.title: Evaluate expressions when computing numeric imbalance
matchstick.principle: Before comparing the two sides, fully evaluate any arithmetic expressions (e.g., ‘XI + I’) to obtain the numeric values of each side.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the start of solving any matchstick equation, after reading the equation.
matchstick.example: Comparing the left and right sides as strings without evaluating the addition, missing the true numeric imbalance.

matchstick.title: Transfer I stick across equality
matchstick.principle: When the numeric imbalance is exactly 2, move a vertical I‑stick from a numeral on the side with excess to a numeral on the side with deficit, crossing the equality sign.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the imbalance is 2 and there is an I that can be moved across the equality sign without invalidating either numeral.
matchstick.example: Moving an I across the equality sign but leaving the source numeral without any I, making it invalid.

matchstick.title: Reposition I before X to change XI to IX
matchstick.principle: If a numeral ‘XI’ appears, moving its I‑stick to the left of the X changes it to ‘IX’, decreasing its value by 2.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to reduce a side by 2 and a ‘XI’ is present.
matchstick.example: Moving the I from ‘XI’ but placing it incorrectly, creating an invalid numeral.

matchstick.title: Convert '+' to '=' by moving its vertical stick
matchstick.principle: If a '+' operator is present, you can turn it into a valid '=' by removing its vertical stick, leaving the two horizontal sticks which form an equals sign. The removed vertical stick must be placed somewhere that does not alter any numeral (e.g., overlapping an existing vertical stick) to satisfy the single‑stick move rule.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation contains a '+' and you need to replace it with '=', and the '+' consists of a vertical and a horizontal stick.
matchstick.example: Changing '+' to '=', but also moving the removed vertical stick onto a numeral, unintentionally altering its value and breaking the equality.

matchstick.description: Moving a stick from a numeral that cannot lose a stick without becoming invalid (e.g., X, V, solitary I)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model assumes any stick can be removed, ignoring the structural requirements of certain numerals.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Check that the source numeral will remain a valid Roman numeral after the stick is removed.

matchstick.description: Providing an invalid equation after moving a stick (including incomplete or unreachable solutions)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on the move itself and neglects the overall syntactic validity of the resulting expression.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After moving a stick, verify that every character (numeral and operator) is still a valid Roman numeral or operator.

matchstick.description: Moving a stick from the equality sign and leaving no valid '=' sign in the equation
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model may try to repurpose a horizontal stick from '=', not realizing that '=' must retain two horizontals.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: If you take a stick from '=', ensure the remaining two horizontals are still present; otherwise keep '=' unchanged.

matchstick.description: Not verifying numeric equality after transformation; resulting equation may be syntactically valid but numerically false
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model stops after producing a visually correct equation, forgetting to recompute the arithmetic.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always evaluate both sides of the final equation to confirm numeric equality.

matchstick.description: Moving more than one stick (or removing multiple sticks) violates the single‑stick rule
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model sometimes treats a multi‑step adjustment as a single move.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Count the sticks you relocate; only one stick may be moved from its original position to a new one.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model may think adding a diagonal slash creates a distinct operator, but the puzzle rules forbid any transformation that results in '≠'.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Never add a diagonal to the equality sign; if you modify '=', ensure it remains two horizontal sticks forming a valid '='.
